subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should automatic sensitive-value sanitization for final agent/channel output be a core security boundary, a plugin/ClawHub capability built on outbound hooks, or intentionally out of scope beyond the current log/transcript/tool redaction boundaries?
rationale: Source inspection shows the gap, but the requested behavior changes visible agent output, security expectations, and config policy, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Define Narrow Core Boundary
options.body: Approve a scoped core design for final-output redaction that reuses existing helpers, documents defaults/exceptions, and adds regression coverage for final replies and channel payloads.

options.title: Route To Plugin
options.body: Treat this as an optional sanitizer plugin using reply_payload_sending or message_sending hooks, with ClawHub packaging and smoke proof rather than a new core config surface.

options.title: Keep Current Boundary
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, diagnostics, tool payloads, and internal-scaffolding cleanup as the supported core redaction boundary and close or narrow broader output-sanitization requests.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Core Boundary
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped core design for final-output redaction that reuses existing helpers, documents defaults/exceptions, and adds regression coverage for final replies and channel payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS makes this owner group the clearest route for security-sensitive config and secret-handling policy.
